neighbours.label: the material word of a rough, traditional or makeshift dwelling (earth lodge, sod house, tar-paper shack, adobe)
fire: The Pawnee built round earth lodges with a smoke hole in the roof.
Homesteaders without timber cut prairie turf to build a sod house.
The camp's families shared drafty tar paper shacks through the winter.
Each Arikara village held dozens of earth lodges near the river.
The pioneer family spent their first winter in a dugout sod shelter.
Coal miners lived in rough log cabins chinked with mud.
The Hopi still live in adobe dwellings stacked on the mesa.
Their earthen pit houses were dug three feet into the ground.
quiet: The developers built round glass towers with a garden on the roof.
Young professionals without savings rented a studio apartment downtown.
The resort's families shared spacious timeshare condos through the winter.
Each suburban street held dozens of brick houses near the park.
The young family spent their first winter in a rented duplex.
Bank managers lived in large stone mansions on the hill.
The executives still live in concrete high-rises downtown.
Their steel-framed office towers were finished three months early.
